```{r, include = FALSE}
# the full examples run when the package is built; CRAN checks skip them for time
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true"), collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(bayescompR)
# chains run in parallel on this many cores; on your own machine use
# options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
options(mc.cores = 2)
```

The parser and semantic analyzer of bayescompR do not depend on how a
model is executed. They produce a typed, versioned intermediate
representation (IR). A backend turns the IR into the functions the
inference algorithms call. The R backend in this package is always
available; the native backends compile the same IR to machine code. They
are built from the
[bayescomp-native-rs](https://github.com/adamrsophie/bayescomp-native-rs)
repository.

## Installing a native backend

bayescompR itself has no compiled code. `bayescomp_install_backend()`
downloads the prebuilt shared library of a backend for your operating
system and architecture from the releases of bayescomp-native-rs, checks
its checksum and stores it in `tools::R_user_dir("bayescompR", "data")`.
The backend is registered at once and again whenever bayescompR is loaded;
nothing is downloaded unless you call the function.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bayescomp_install_backend("cranelift")
bayescomp_install_backend("llvm")
bayescomp_backends()
```

| Backend | Prebuilt libraries | LLVM installation needed |
|---------|--------------------|--------------------------|
| `"r"` | not needed | no |
| `"cranelift"` | Linux (x86_64, aarch64), macOS (arm64, x86_64), Windows (x86_64) | no |
| `"llvm"` | Linux (x86_64), macOS (arm64) | no; LLVM is linked into the library |

The Cranelift libraries need glibc 2.28 or newer on Linux and macOS 11 or
newer. The LLVM libraries need glibc 2.35 or newer, libstdc++, zlib, zstd
and libxml2 (`libxml2.so.2`) on Linux; on macOS they are built and tested
on macOS 15. Each download is checked against its SHA-256 checksum, which
needs R 4.5 or newer; on older versions of R, install from a file with
`path =`.

When no prebuilt library is published for a platform, the function says
so. Build the library with Rust instead and install it from a file with
`bayescomp_install_backend(path = )`:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/adamrsophie/bayescomp-native-rs
cd bayescomp-native-rs
cargo build --release -p bcn-ffi --features cranelift
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# libbcn_ffi.so on Linux, libbcn_ffi.dylib on macOS, bcn_ffi.dll on Windows
bayescomp_install_backend("cranelift", path = "target/release/libbcn_ffi.so")
```

`bayescomp_remove_backend()` deletes an installed library.

`options(bayescompR.native_engine = "interpreter")` runs the native
runtime's reference interpreter instead of the JIT compiler, which is
useful to tell a code generation problem from a runtime one. In this version the
native backends provide the log density and its gradient; the native
lowering does not yet cover user defined functions, truncation, matrix
division and a few other constructs, and such programs are refused with
`bayescomp_unsupported_error` when the model is built. An evaluation in
native code cannot be interrupted, so a `while` loop that never ends blocks
the R session.

```{r}
bayescomp_backends()
```

## The IR

`bayescomp_ir()` returns the IR as R lists or as JSON:

```{r}
code <- "
functions { real twice(real x) { return 2 * x; } }
data { int N; vector[N] y; }
parameters { real<lower=0> sigma; }
model { y ~ normal(twice(0.5), sigma); }"
ir <- bayescomp_ir(code)
ir$ir_version
names(ir$blocks)
```

### Schema, version 1.0.0

The document is an object with three members:

* `ir_version`: the schema version, a semantic version string.
* `stan_version`: the language version implemented, `"2.40.0"`.
* `blocks`: an object with one member per program block that is present,
  named `functions`, `data`, `transformed data`, `parameters`,
  `transformed parameters`, `model` and `generated quantities`.

Every node is an object with a `kind` and a source location `loc`
(`line`, `col`). Blocks have `kind = "block"`, a `name` and a `body` (array
of statements).

**Types.** Declared types (`type` of a `decl`) have `base` (`int`, `real`,
`complex`, `vector`, `row_vector`, `matrix`, their complex versions,
`tuple`, or a constrained type such as `simplex` or
`cholesky_factor_corr`), `adims` (array size expressions), `sizes`
(vector or matrix size expressions) and `cons` (constraint arguments:
`lower`, `upper`, `offset`, `multiplier`). Value types of expressions
(`type` of an expression) have `base` (`int`, `real`, `complex`,
`vector`, `row_vector`, `matrix`, `complex_vector`, `complex_row_vector`,
`complex_matrix` or `tuple`, whose element types are in `elems`) and
`nd`, the number of array dimensions.

**Declarations.** `kind = "decl"` with `name`, `type`, `block`, `top`
(declared at block level) and optional `init`.

**Expressions.** Every expression has `type` and `data_only` (`true` when
it depends only on data). A backend must use `data_only`, not the run time
value, to decide which terms of a density `propto` drops: a term is kept
when any argument it depends on is neither `data_only` nor an integer, as
in Stan. A backend can also hoist `data_only` expressions. Kinds:

| kind | members |
|------|---------|
| `int`, `real` | `value` |
| `imag` | `value` (an imaginary literal such as `2.5i`) |
| `string` | `value` (only in `print`, `reject`, `fatal_error`) |
| `var` | `name`, `origin` (the block, or `argument`, `local`, `loop`) |
| `binop` | `op` (`+ - * / %/% % \ .* ./ ^ .^ == != < <= > >= && ||`), `a`, `b` |
| `unop` | `op` (`-`, `!`, `+`), `a` |
| `transpose` | `a` (postfix `'`) |
| `paren` | `a` |
| `cond` | `cond`, `a`, `b` (the `?:` operator) |
| `call` | `name`, `args`, `cond_bar`, `sig`, `resolved` |
| `index` | `x`, `idx`; each index has `kind` `single` (`e`, an int), `intarray` (`e`, an int array), `range` (`lo`, `hi`), `lower` (`lo`, for `a:`), `upper` (`hi`, for `:b`) or `omni` |
| `array_expr`, `rowvec_expr` | `items` (`{...}` and `[...]` literals) |
| `tuple_expr` | `items` (a tuple literal `(a, b)`) |
| `proj` | `x`, `k` (element `k` of a tuple, `x.k`) |

**Resolved signatures.** Calls and sampling statements carry `sig`: the
function `name`, whether it is `user` defined, the `mangled` name of a user
function overload, the argument types `args` and the return type `ret`.
Library signatures use Stan's argument patterns (`reals`, `ints`,
`vectors` and so on), which tells a backend which vectorized kernel to use.

**Statements.** `assign` (`lhs`, `op` such as `=` or `+=`, `rhs`),
`tilde` (`lhs`, `dist`, `args`, `trunc` with `lo` and `hi`, `fname` naming
the `_lupdf` or `_lupmf` implementation, `sig`), `target_add` and
`jacobian_add` (`value`), `for` (`var`, `lo`, `hi`, `body`), `foreach`
(`var`, `iter`, `body`), `while` (`cond`, `body`), `if` (`cond`, `then`,
`els`), `block_stmt` (`body`, and `profile`, the name of a `profile`
block, when it is one), `unpack` (`lhs`, a `tuple_expr` of variables,
and `rhs`), `break`, `continue`, `return` (`value`),
`print`, `reject` and `fatal_error` (`items`), `call_stmt` (`call`) and
`empty`. Function definitions have `kind = "fundef"`, `name`, `rtype`,
`args` (each with `name`, `type`, `data_only`), `body` and `sig`.

```{r}
cat(substr(bayescomp_ir(code, json = TRUE), 1, 400), "...\n")
```

### Versioning

The IR follows semantic versioning. Adding optional members raises the
minor version; renaming or removing members, or changing their meaning,
raises the major version. A backend declares the IR versions it accepts and
bayescompR refuses to use a backend that does not accept the current one.

## The backend interface

A backend package calls `bayescomp_register_backend()` in its `.onLoad()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bayescomp_register_backend(
  name = "mybackend",
  capabilities = c("log_density", "gradient"),
  ir_versions = "1.0.0",
  compile = function(ir, model) {
    # ir: the list returned by bayescomp_ir(); model: the data bound model,
    # whose element `data` holds the data and whose transformed data have
    # already been computed by the R backend.
    list(
      log_density_gradient = function(u, jacobian, propto) {
        list(value = 0, grad = numeric(length(u)))
      },
      log_density = function(u, jacobian, propto) 0   # optional
    )
  },
  description = "An example backend")
```

`log_density_gradient(u, jacobian, propto)` receives the unconstrained
parameter vector and returns the log density and its gradient with the same
conventions as `bayescomp_log_prob()`: the Jacobian of the constraining
transforms is included when `jacobian` is `TRUE`, and constant terms of
sampling statements are dropped when `propto` is `TRUE`. Points outside the
support return `-Inf`; a `reject()` in the program raises a condition of
class `bayescomp_reject_error`.

`bayescomp_native_inputs(model)` returns what a compiled backend needs:
the IR as a JSON string, the values of every data and transformed data
variable (computed by the R implementation and flattened in Stan order)
as JSON, and the number of unconstrained parameters. A native runtime
reports errors as strings with a code prefix (`"E_DOMAIN: scale is
negative"`, `"E_REJECT: ..."`, `"E_FATAL: ..."`, `"E_SHAPE: ..."`,
`"E_UNSUPPORTED: ..."`), and
`bayescomp_native_error()` turns them into the condition classes of the R
backend, so the samplers reject a proposal the same way whichever backend
raised the error.

```{r}
m_native <- bayescomp_model("data { int N; vector[N] y; } transformed data { real m = mean(y); }
                             parameters { real mu; } model { y ~ normal(mu, 1); }",
                            data = list(N = 3, y = c(0.2, 1.1, 0.7)))
inputs <- bayescomp_native_inputs(m_native)
str(inputs, max.level = 1)
cat(inputs$data, "\n")
e <- tryCatch(bayescomp_native_error("E_DOMAIN: scale is negative"), error = identity)
class(e)
conditionMessage(e)
```

### Capability negotiation

The capabilities are `log_density`, `gradient`, `constrain` (the
constraining transforms and transformed parameters for output),
`generated_quantities` and `rng`. `log_density` and `gradient` are
required. When a backend lacks one of the others, the R implementation can
provide it, but only when the user asks:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
m <- bayescomp_model(code, data, backend = "cranelift")
#> Error: backend 'cranelift' does not provide constrain, generated_quantities, rng;
#>   set allow_fallback = TRUE to use the R implementation for them
m <- bayescomp_model(code, data, backend = "cranelift", allow_fallback = TRUE)
m$provenance   # which backend provides each capability
```

Implementations are never mixed silently.

### Validation

`bayescomp_validate_backend()` evaluates the log density and gradient of a
native model and of the R implementation at random points and reports the
differences. Every backend package runs it in its tests on a corpus of
models, and the benchmark scripts compare total inference time.

Here is the whole interface exercised with a toy backend that implements
one model by hand:

```{r}
bayescomp_register_backend("toy", c("log_density", "gradient"), "1.0.0",
  compile = function(ir, model) list(
    log_density_gradient = function(u, jacobian, propto) {
      # propto = TRUE drops the constant terms, as the R backend does
      list(value = if (propto) -(u - 1)^2 / 8 else dnorm(u, 1, 2, log = TRUE),
           grad = -(u - 1) / 4)
    }))
m <- bayescomp_model("parameters { real mu; } model { mu ~ normal(1, 2); }",
                     backend = "toy", allow_fallback = TRUE)
unlist(m$provenance)
v <- bayescomp_validate_backend(m, n = 5)
max(v$lp_abs, v$grad_abs)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
rm("toy", envir = bayescompR:::.backends)
```

## Accelerators

GPU, TPU and NPU execution is planned for version 0.2.0 through a backend
that lowers the IR to jaxR (StableHLO compiled by XLA through PJRT, which
covers CUDA, ROCm, TPU, Metal and vendor NPU plugins). The IR already
carries the static types and shapes that such a lowering needs.
